_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with previously treated, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with an FGFR2 fusion or other rearrangement as detected by an FDA-approved test

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, non-randomized, single-arm, multicenter (international), multi-cohort trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with previously treated, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with an FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement; all had received at least 1 prior line of systemic therapy (32% had 2 prior lines, 29% had 3 or more)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DoR) as determined by blinded independent central review (BICR) per RECIST
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 23% (95% CI 16, 32) by BICR, including 1 (1%) CR and 24 (22%) PR; median DoR 5.0 months (95% CI 3.7, 9.3)

key_safety: Most common (>=20%) adverse reactions were nail toxicity, stomatitis, dry eye, fatigue, alopecia, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia syndrome, arthralgia, dysgeusia, constipation, abdominal pain, dry mouth, eyelash changes, diarrhea, dry skin, decreased appetite, vision blurred and vomiting. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 32% of patients; fatal adverse reactions occurred in 1 (0.9%) patient (sepsis).
target_moa: Small molecule ATP-competitive kinase inhibitor of fibroblast growth factor receptors (FGFRs) 1, 2, and 3
companion_dx_detail: Foundation Medicine companion diagnostic assay (FoundationOne CDx / F1CDx) to select patients with cholangiocarcinoma harboring an FGFR2 gene fusion or other select rearrangement

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the Division did not obtain the advice of the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) because no review issues raised significant public health questions regarding the risk:benefit assessment

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response

summary.text: Truseltiq received Priority review and was granted accelerated approval under 21 CFR Subpart H based on overall response rate and duration of response from the single-arm Study CBGJ398X2204, with a required confirmatory randomized trial comparing infigratinib to chemotherapy. The drug had prior Fast Track Designation (September 10, 2019) and Orphan Designation (September 11, 2019) for cholangiocarcinoma.
